minutes.headline: Board heard LED streetlight options and a Flat Hill Road drainage dispute, then went into executive session on land.
minutes.summary: The Select Board welcomed a new member, approved a Boys and Girls Club toll booth drive, and heard a Green Communities presentation on LED streetlight conversion with buy-versus-lease options. It spent the longest stretch on Flat Hill Road water drainage, where town counsel said the town has no liability and the board backed a maintenance letter to the village association. The meeting ended with a vote to enter executive session on two Gilchrist Street parcels.

public_comment.topic: Land-use director asked for a letter of support for a 319 grant application for stormwater practices in the upper watershed, and announced a Planning Board hearing on adult-use marijuana regulations on June 25.
Thanked election candidates, noted low turnout, and urged clearing brush and old playground equipment behind the primary school lot for abutters.
Raised the pond in Cortland Circle, the flooded lot at 252 Flat Hill Road, road paving durability, and asked for an engineering firm to evaluate.

what_happened.line: The Select Board heard a Green Communities presentation on converting streetlights to LED, with options to buy from Unitil, buy from a private installer, or do nothing.
On Flat Hill Road drainage, the board reached consensus to support a maintenance letter to the Village at Flat Hill association and to ask town groups to review water impacts.
The board voted to approve the Boys and Girls Club toll booth drive on June 9 at Town Center.
Buying the LED lights would likely need borrowing by town meeting vote, because the capital plan has no money set aside for it.
The meeting ended with a vote to enter executive session on two Gilchrist Street parcels.

why_it_matters: Streetlight costs are paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, so the buy-or-lease choice would set the yearly bill and may put a borrowing article before town meeting voters.
The Flat Hill Road drainage question touches nearby property owners and the town's stormwater, conservation and planning work, and the board has not yet set any town spending to address it.
watch_next: Next Select Board meeting on June 5 (organization discussion), with a goal-setting workshop on the 12th.
Planning Board hearing on adult-use marijuana regulations on June 25.
